results.title: 75+ employee productivity statistics for 2026 - Superhuman Blog
results.content: Employee productivity statistics reveal a workplace at a crossroads: only [21% of employees globally are engaged](https://www.gallup.com/workplace/349484/state-of-the-global-workplace.aspx?ref=blog.superhuman.com), yet organizations implementing the right strategies are seeing remarkable gains. *   Engaged employees are [18% more productive](https://www.gallup.com/workplace/285674/improve-employee-engagement-workplace.aspx?ref=blog.superhuman.com), leading to 23% higher profits. *   Remote workers demonstrate [35-40% higher productivity](https://www.activtrak.com/solutions/productivity-management/workplace-productivity-statistics?ref=blog.superhuman.com) than in-office employees, with 40% fewer mistakes. *   Engaged employees are [18% more productive](https://www.gallup.com/workplace/285674/improve-employee-engagement-workplace.aspx?ref=blog.superhuman.com), leading to 23% higher profits. *   Employees are[2.6x more likely](https://www.gallup.com/workplace/691643/work-nearly-doubled-two-years.aspx?ref=blog.superhuman.com) to feel comfortable using AI when leadership communicates a clear integration plan. *   Employees lose[103 hours annually](https://www.electroiq.com/stats/productivity-in-the-workplace-statistics/?ref=blog.superhuman.com) to unnecessary meetings alone. With[40% of employees](https://www.gallup.com/workplace/653286/americans-using-workplace-nearly-doubled-past-year.aspx?ref=blog.superhuman.com) now using AI and potential time savings of[5 hours weekly](https://www.adeccogroup.com/future-of-work/latest-research/global-workforce-of-the-future-2024/?ref=blog.superhuman.com), technology adoption is critical—but only[one-third of organizations](https://www.mckinsey.com/capabilities/quantumblack/our-insights/the-state-of-ai?ref=blog.superhuman.com) have scaled successfully. With[39% of skills](https://www.weforum.org/publications/the-future-of-jobs-report-2025/?ref=blog.superhuman.com) changing by 2030 and[94% of employees](https://learning.linkedin.com/resources/workplace-learning-report?ref=blog.superhuman.com) willing to stay longer for learning opportunities, development programs are productivity multipliers. These employee productivity statistics reveal significant challenges, from [21% global engagement](https://www.gallup.com/workplace/349484/state-of-the-global-workplace.aspx?ref=blog.superhuman.com) to [275 daily interruptions](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/worklab/work-trend-index/breaking-down-infinite-workday?ref=blog.superhuman.com), but the solutions are clear.

results.content: Attend a SHRM state event to network with other HR professionals and learn more about the future of work. The findings from the highly anticipated annual reports, 2026 State of the Workplace, and 2026 CHRO Priorities and Perspectives, indicate while the adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) is accelerating, the true engine of organizational resilience remains human leadership and culture. Though workers, HR professionals, and HR executives agree that salaries and burnout are leading concerns, employers highlight effective leadership and management as their primary workplace need. * **Rising Worker Expectations: 72%** of HR professionals and HR executives report that workers have higher expectations of employers today, highlighting the growing need for organizations to adapt to evolving demands. HR professionals: A sample of 1,856 HR professionals was surveyed between Oct. 24 and Nov. 6, 2025, using SHRM’s Voice of Work Research Panel. **2026 CHRO Priorities and Perspectives:** A sample of 129 CHROs or those who sit as the senior-most HR professional in their organization were surveyed between Oct. 7 and Nov. 5, 2025.
